text:
asha: Heads-up — onboarding the new reranker model from HF shows embedding mismatches vs our Redwood conversion. Quick repro: embeddings drift ~1.2 L2 on our eval set after conversion + quantization. Suspect tokenization/pooling differences.

tom: Can you paste the HF config/tokenizer bits you used for conversion? also which pooling did you expect (cls vs mean)?

asha: Pasting minimal snippets I used for the conversion: 
```
# tokenizer config.json (from HF)
{"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "unk_token": "<unk>", "model_max_length": 2048, "truncation_side": "right"}
```
And the small conversion shim I ran: 
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf-reranker-x')
# convert to redwood format (naive)
redwood_tok = { 'vocab': t.get_vocab(), 'special_tokens': t.special_tokens_map }
```
I then set pooling to "cls" in Redwood's embed config.

joel: Two likely issues: 1) HF model uses an explicit [CLS] pooling token vs HF tokenizer using <s> as BOS; our conversion expects pooler_token id stored in special_tokens_map["cls_token"]. If that mapping is missing we end up pooling on the first token (which may be padding after truncation). 2) truncation_side vs our default behavior. Redwood inference pipeline historically used truncation_side='left' for rerankers to keep suffix; HF config says 'right' so token windows differ.

asha: Ah — I did not copy special_tokens_map keys exactly. HF had "cls_token": "<s>", but my conversion wrote it under "bos_token" only.

tom: That would do it. Quick check: run this to compare token ids for a sample prompt on both sides: 
```bash
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf-reranker-x')
print('HF ids:', t.encode('Search query example', add_special_tokens=True))
# then run the same through the redwood-converted tokenizer (or dump your converted json and load similarly)
PY
```
If the CLS id differs you'll see shifted tokens.

asha: Ran that — HF ids: [1, 234, 56, 2] (1=bos/cls), our converted -> [0, 234, 56, 2] (0 is PAD in our mapping). So we were pooling on pad. Oof.

joel: That matches what I expected. Also check truncation: HF said truncation_side='right' so if your conversion defaulted to 'left' the tokens kept for long inputs differ, which hurts reranker heavily.

asha: Quick mitigation applied: fixed special_tokens_map to include "cls_token": "<s>", forced truncation_side='right' in the conversion manifest, and re-ran quantization (int8). Embedding L2 delta dropped from ~1.2 to ~0.06 on the small eval set. 

ci-bot: [deploy] conversion-fix branch pushed to origin/eng-ml/convert-tokenizer-fixes (CI:unit tests running) :white_check_mark:

tom: Nice. Follow-ups: 
- Add explicit test that token ids for sample sentences match HF after conversion.
- Persist special_tokens_map keys: cls_token, pad_token, bos_token, eos_token, unk_token.
- Record truncation_side and model_max_length in conversion metadata so runtime mirrors HF.

joel: Also add a small script in the onboarding checklist to assert pooling_strategy: if model has pooler_token map to a real non-pad id, set pooling_strategy='cls', otherwise fallback to 'mean' with a warning. That avoids silent pad-pooling regressions.

asha: I'll open a PR with tests and the checklist notes. For the quant experiments: be careful — even with token mapping correct, int8 kernels occasionally shift logits slightly; add a monitoring eval that compares embedding drift post-quant. If drift > 0.2 L2 trigger rollback.

tom: Agreed. Thanks for catching this early — saved us from shipping a subtle reranker regression. :thumbsup:

asha: Thanks all — sending the PR now.
